input.question: Alright, so we all know most Hollywood films get history wrong, but are there any Hollywood blockbusters that are very historically accurate?
input.ground_truth: Master and Commander is both a really good movie, and actually historically accurate, to an extent. I've watched it, and I didn't see any particular inaccuracies about life onboard a wooden warship. The plot is based off of the British chase of the American commerce raider [U.S.S *Essex*](_URL_0_) during the War of 1812, which sailed down the eastern coast of Brazil, then up into the Pacific where it destroyed the British whaling industry. Of course, Americans don't want to see Americans as the bad guys in films, so they made the antagonist a French ship, but still.

Question: Alright, so we all know most Hollywood films get history wrong, but are there any Hollywood blockbusters that are very historically accurate?

response.prediction:
Okay, let’s imagine you have a big box of LEGO bricks, and you want to build a real castle, just like the one people built a long, long time ago. But sometimes, when people make big movies, like about knights or soldiers, they use some blueprints that aren’t exactly right—they add extra bricks or leave some out, so it doesn’t look exactly like the real thing.

But sometimes, some big movies try really, really hard to use the right bricks and build things just like they were in real life. These movies try to show clothes, buildings, and even how people talked, almost like it really happened.

For example, the movie “Dunkirk” about World War II airplanes and boats tries very hard to look like what really happened. Another one is “Schindler’s List,” which tries to show what life was like for people during a very sad time in history.

But even in those movies, sometimes they still change a little bit to make the story easier to follow or more exciting, just like how you might change a LEGO castle a tiny bit to make it cooler.

So, some big movies try really hard to be like real history, but not all of them are perfect. Most add a little magic or change things to make the story fun!
